stories.headline: OpenAI Put ChatGPT Inside Epic's Charts. It Can Read 325 Million Patients and Write Nothing.
stories.key_takeaway: OpenAI connected ChatGPT for Healthcare to Epic on Sept. 1, giving clinicians read-only access to authorized records covering more than 325 million patients — a write lock that protects the database but not the clinical decision.

pull_quote.text: By bringing relevant information together more quickly and comprehensively, the technology has the potential to reduce time spent synthesizing data and give clinicians more time with patients.

stories.article_excerpt: On Sept. 1, OpenAI crossed a line American health IT has spent a decade fortifying: it put a general-purpose chatbot in the chart.

stories.headline: South Korea Is Not Building a Data Center. It Is Building 18.4 Gigawatts.
stories.key_takeaway: South Korea has committed roughly $919 billion across chips, robotics and compute and is procuring gigawatts, land rights and tariff relief rather than a single flagship campus, but its sovereign AI stack still depends on American accelerators.

pull_quote.text: Semiconductors, physical AI, and AI data centers are the triple axis for our great leap forward.

stories.article_excerpt: When President Lee Jae-myung addressed the nation on June 29, he did not unveil a campus. He unveiled a power budget.

stories.headline: The Justice Department Filed on OpenAI's Side. The Judge Still Decides.
stories.key_takeaway: The DOJ's first statement of interest in an AI copyright case urges the court to find that LLM training is fair use, but the filing binds no one and reaches only training, leaving the Times's data-acquisition and output claims untouched.

pull_quote.text: is siding with a handful of trillion-dollar AI companies at the expense of the countless American creators whose work they stole

stories.article_excerpt: On Tuesday, Sept. 1, the United States told a federal judge in Manhattan what it believes copyright law says about training.

stories.headline: AfterQuery Went From $300 Million to $3.2 Billion in Five Months. It Sells Training Data.
stories.key_takeaway: AfterQuery's reported 10.7x valuation jump in five months shows that expert human judgment, sold as datasets and RL environments, has become the scarcest input in frontier AI.

pull_quote.text: Human data is an enormous market and critical bottleneck for frontier models, and for advancing the quality of AI.

stories.article_excerpt: In April, a San Francisco startup barely a year old announced it was worth $300 million. On September 1, that number moved.

stories.headline: Kirkland & Ellis Decided Not to Buy Legal AI. It Is Spending $500 Million to Build It.
stories.key_takeaway: The world's highest-grossing law firm is spending $500 million of its own revenue to own its AI workflows outright, betting that licensed tools only raise an industry baseline that erodes no one's competitive edge.

pull_quote.text: While the use of widely available AI tools was raising the floor for everyone in the legal industry, Kirkland had to do more because we don't get hired for the floor.

stories.article_excerpt: The world's highest-grossing law firm has just told the legal AI industry that its products are table stakes.

stories.headline: Palo Alto Paid $500 Million for Console. The Real Winner May Be the Startup It Left Behind.
stories.key_takeaway: Palo Alto Networks' reported $500 million purchase of two-year-old Console, roughly triple its $157 million private valuation, removes the last direct rival to Sequoia-backed Serval in AI-native IT service automation.

pull_quote.text: This is the shift to software-as-an-agent, giving our platform the arms and legs to deliver autonomous security outcomes across the entire enterprise.
pull_quote.role: Chairman and CEO, Palo Alto Networks

stories.article_excerpt: Palo Alto Networks bought a two-year-old company with $29 million in venture funding for roughly $500 million.

stories.headline: Uber Spent a Decade Fighting Driver Unions. Now It Is Lobbying Beside Them Against Robotaxis.
stories.key_takeaway: Uber is lobbying alongside the driver unions it fought for a decade to force human-driver quotas and hybrid-network rules on robotaxi operators, a coalition that protects the platform's distribution position at least as much as it protects drivers.

pull_quote.text: If you do driving for a living, you should be concerned about Waymo coming into our city.

data_points.label: Drivers displaced per AV, Uber estimate

stories.article_excerpt: For ten years, Uber spent hundreds of millions of dollars keeping its drivers from organizing. That fight is now over.

stories.headline: Anthropic Wants to Monitor Misuse Without Holding the Logs. Banks Keep the Keys.
stories.key_takeaway: Anthropic's Enterprise Frontier Safeguards splits custody from computation, letting regulated customers keep misuse-monitoring logs under their own keys while Anthropic runs the detection — but it shifts triage labor and verification burden onto the customer.

pull_quote.text: Enterprise Frontier Safeguards gives us exactly what we asked for: our logs stay in a Wells-managed environment under Wells-managed keys. We keep custody of our data while Anthropic operates the detection.
pull_quote.role: Chief Information Security Officer, Wells Fargo

stories.article_excerpt: For a year, Anthropic has told its largest customers that frontier models are dangerous enough to require surveillance.

stories.headline: Meta Says Muse Spark Scores 98.1% at a Million Tokens. The Weights Are Coming, the Paper Is Not.
stories.key_takeaway: Meta's promised open-weights Muse Spark rides on a self-reported 98.1% MRCR score roughly 22 points above the best independently documented result, measured in a reasoning mode users could not access at launch, on a benchmark researchers say is trivially overfit.

pull_quote.text: only including this as a long context benchmark is somewhat misleading since meta likely overfit very hard on it

stories.article_excerpt: Mark Zuckerberg promised on X on September 2 that Meta will release an open-weights version of Muse Spark. Then came the asterisks.

stories.headline: Alibaba Did Not Make Qwen Bigger. It Made It 22 CodeArena Points Better.
stories.key_takeaway: Alibaba lifted Qwen3.8-Max to the top of the CodeArena WebDev board with post-training alone — no change to its 2.4T parameters, 1M context or price — and the 22-point gain sits inside the leaderboard's own error bars.

pull_quote.text: Qwen3.8-Max-0902 jumps from 1669 to 1691, setting a new record for agentic coding (WebDev) workflows, with standout strength in multistep reasoning, tool use, and full app generation.

stories.article_excerpt: Alibaba shipped a new flagship coding model on September 2 and forgot to make it bigger. That was the point.

stories.headline: NVIDIA Built a Hospital in Simulation So Its Robots Could Practice Somewhere Safe
stories.key_takeaway: NVIDIA open-sourced a four-part healthcare robotics stack built around the admission that real clinical training data is too scarce and too dangerous to collect, betting instead on synthetic hospitals — and leaving the regulatory gap between a simulation benchmark and a cleared device entirely untouched.

pull_quote.text: This project addresses the physical AI deployment paradox. Autonomous systems need real-world experience to become safe, but they must be safe before they can gain real-world experience.

stories.article_excerpt: The hardest problem in clinical robotics was never the robot. It is that nobody will let an unproven machine near a patient.

stories.headline: CrowdStrike Set Two AI Agents Loose on a Copy of Your Network. Neither One Is Supposed to Win.
stories.key_takeaway: CrowdStrike's SafeMind runs an offensive model in a continuous loop against a defensive one inside a telemetry-derived digital twin of a customer network, but the evaluation numbers are self-reported and no general availability date or pricing has been announced.

pull_quote.text: The future of cybersecurity won't be defined by AI that simply identifies threats, it will be defined by AI that defeats them.

stories.article_excerpt: Somewhere in CrowdStrike's cloud, a model called Red Tempest is working its way through a replica of a customer's network.

stories.headline: 4.5 Billion TikTok Records Are Sitting on Hugging Face. The Only Thing Stopping Misuse Is a Dataset Card.
stories.key_takeaway: A lone researcher put 4.5 billion TikTok video records on Hugging Face in a 289GB dataset whose only guardrail against identification, profiling and targeting is unenforceable text on the dataset card.

pull_quote.text: Individuals lose control of their personal information when it is scraped without their knowledge and against their expectations.
pull_quote.role: Joint statement on data scraping, signed by 12 authorities

stories.article_excerpt: On the largest public repository of machine learning artifacts on the internet sits roughly 289 gigabytes of other people's lives.

stories.headline: Anker Put 26 TOPS and 48 Terabytes in a Box So Your Camera Footage Never Leaves the House
stories.key_takeaway: Anker's MindBase moves home-security inference onto a swappable 26-TOPS card with up to 48TB of local storage and no subscription, but the hub has no price or ship date and the company's 2022-23 encryption scandal means its local-only claims need independent verification.

pull_quote.text: We believe the autonomous home needs three things: connection, local intelligence and memory that stays in the home under the family's control.

stories.article_excerpt: The most interesting thing Anker showed at IFA Berlin on September 3 was not a camera. It was a card you can pull out.

stories.headline: Astra Thinks in a Loop Instead of in Words. That Is Exactly What Worries the Safety Researchers.
stories.key_takeaway: OpenAI's Astra does part of its reasoning in unreadable latent vectors rather than legible tokens, and safety researchers fear the precedent will erode chain-of-thought monitoring across the industry even if Astra's own use stays bounded.

pull_quote.text: My biggest concern is that a natural progression from here would involve scaling up the opaque reasoning to the point where the model reasons entirely or almost entirely in latent space.

stories.article_excerpt: For three years the industry's most reassuring answer to what a frontier model is doing has been the same: read its thoughts.

stories.headline: Google's Answer to Canva Removes the Canvas
stories.key_takeaway: Google Pics ships prompt-first image creation into Workspace with no free tier, betting that generative models make the design canvas optional — while Canva's $42B business argues the last 20% still needs human hands.

pull_quote.text: Pics eliminates the frustration of wrangling pixels and feeling like you need to be a graphic designer to deliver a great image.

stories.article_excerpt: Google shipped a design tool on September 1 that does not, strictly speaking, let you design.

stories.headline: Two Automated Systems, One Case: AI Searched 80,000 Cameras, Then AI Wrote the Report
stories.key_takeaway: A Texas sheriff's report on a nationwide license-plate-reader search was itself partly written by Axon's Draft One, chaining two automated systems whose audit trails cannot be used to check each other.

pull_quote.text: There is no meaningful way to audit Draft One usage, whether you're a police chief or an independent researcher, because Axon designed it that way.

stories.article_excerpt: The police report documenting one of the most contested surveillance episodes of the past two years ends with a disclosure.

stories.headline: Washington Took Its Deregulation Pitch to the G20. Brussels Was Writing a New Law.
stories.key_takeaway: The US won G20 consensus on the non-binding Carolina Principles, which urge governments to regulate AI through existing sector rules rather than new AI-specific law, on the same day Brussels sent AI Act compliance requests to more than 30 AI companies.

pull_quote.text: Policymakers do not need to approach each innovation in isolation and should not treat every emerging technology as a first-of-its-kind policy problem.
pull_quote.role: Director, White House Office of Science and Technology Policy

stories.article_excerpt: On Tuesday, September 1, in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, the United States asked the world's largest economies to regulate less.
